📰 UFC Diplomacy: Israel in the Cheap Seats

When your main ally turns his 80th birthday into a cage fight on the White House lawn and calls it a “turning point for American diplomacy,” you know you’re not in a serious movie anymore, you’re in a parody.

“Donald Trump celebrated his 80th birthday with a UFC event on the South Lawn and hailed the Iran agreement as a breakthrough that brings stability to the Middle East,” Israeli media note with a mix of disbelief and anger. For many in Israel, the spectacle felt as strange and cruel as the statement itself.

Because behind the fireworks, Trump’s “peace” with Tehran looks a lot like a quit notice. Washington rushed into a deal to end a war it was never ready to sustain, handing Iran immediate oil export relief and financial breathing room, while promising that the “real” nuclear concessions will somehow come later. That’s not strategy, that’s an exit package with branding.

And who pays for this birthday show? Israel, front row, full price. Jerusalem is already furious that Washington is pressuring it to “limit” operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon so as not to upset the negotiations with Iran. 

Don’t finish the job on the militia that Tehran openly arms and funds—because it might ruin the cake-cutting ceremony.

Israeli officials warn that freezing the Lebanon front, letting Hezbollah regroup, and leaving Iran with a survivable nuclear project is not “de-escalation,” it is a countdown to a bloodier, wider war a few years down the line. The message from allies, though, is simple: calm down, sign here, and trust the same regime that sponsors the rockets aimed at you.

So Trump gets his made-for-TV legacy shot: octagon, fireworks, “historic deal.” Iran gets money, time, and strategic depth. The Gulf monarchies get to pretend they live in a “new regional architecture.” And Israel? Israel gets told to sit quietly, absorb the risk, and not embarrass the host on his big birthday.

In this script, “stability” means Washington clocks out, Tehran cashes in, and Israel is left holding the bill for an agreement it didn’t sign but will have to survive. The only real question: when the next war starts, will anyone even remember which UFC card it was announced on?

Do you want the next post on this topic to hit more at Trump personally or more at the Israeli leadership that plays along with him?

🔔 Ripple targets $1B revenue run rate without counting XRP holdings 

❗️ According to posts shared by CoinMarketCap and crypto-focused accounts on X, Ripple expects to end 2026 with a $1 billion revenue run rate. The figure does not include XRP held on Ripple’s balance sheet. That detail matters because Ripple has long faced public debate over the link between its business and XRP. Garlinghouse’s target frames the company as a fintech infrastructure provider that aims to earn money from products, clients, and services, not from token holdings or sales.

🌐 The deal also supports Ripple USD, known as RLUSD. Ripple has promoted the stablecoin for enterprise settlement and collateral use. Recently, crypto news reported that Ripple is also adding RLUSD to new payment tools, including services tied to AI agents and machine payments on the XRP Ledger. Company materials point to custody, treasury management, and liquidity services as core offerings. These products target banks and firms that need faster settlement, account control, and access to digital assets through regulated processes, rather than retail trading.

The Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at its latest meeting, but the signal from Chair Kevin Warsh was enough to rattle markets. Warsh indicated that rate hikes are back on the table if inflation does not continue to ease, a hawkish pivot that caught Wall Street off guard, according to the New York Post.

The FOMC statement flagged inflation as the committee's primary concern, and Warsh's tone in the press conference reinforced that framing. Futures markets, which had been pricing in at least one cut before year-end, shifted quickly - traders are now assigning meaningful probability to a hike scenario.

The move marks a notable departure from the dovish drift that had dominated Fed communication in recent months. Whether this is a genuine recalibration or a warning shot to keep inflation expectations anchored is the question markets will be working through for the next several weeks.

A new update Sl8 has already passed review and will be available on the App Store and Google Play very soon.

In this version, we have added new features for content creators, expanded the app's functionality, and introduced a number of changes that will make it more stable and user-friendly.

📊 Detailed Statistics for Content Creators
The app now features a new Creator Statistics page, where creators can analyze their results, audience activity, and earned revenue in greater detail.

The page will include:
•      interactive charts displaying revenue dynamics;
•      separate income breakdowns for paid posts, post tips, chat tips, and subscriptions;
•      information about top-performing content;
•      a list of top contributing fans;
•      a history of recent purchases, active subscriptions, and sent tips.
With detailed analytics, creators will be able to better understand their audience's activity, see which content generates the most interest, and more accurately evaluate the results of their work.

🛠 Bug Fixes and App Improvements
When preparing a post for publication, hints about media file visibility are now displayed. Before publishing, the creator will be able to see which photos or videos will be visible to all users and which will remain locked.
If age restrictions are enabled while creating a post, an adult content warning will automatically be added to the post cover.

The new version improves chat stability when switching between accounts.
Unread message indicators, notification badges, chat start requests, chat deletion, and various message actions have also been fixed. Additionally, text messages can now be copied.

Special attention was given to image and media file handling. On Android, an issue that could cause images to display incorrectly after cropping has been resolved. Media file uploading has also been fixed, so all selected images should now display correctly.
Scrolling after unlocking paid messages has been improved, and the reliability of feed navigation and filters has been enhanced.
Delays that could occur when editing posts and Layers have been eliminated. Profile updates, the blocked users list, and navigation between different sections of the app have been fixed.

In addition, the team has fixed UI and text rendering across different screen sizes and languages. Accidental repeated report submissions on multiple taps have been resolved, and the performance of notifications, informational messages, and bottom sheets has been improved.
A number of visual issues related to media counters, badges, buttons, and text labels have also been fixed.

The update will be available on the App Store and Google Play very soon.
